claims.text: Docstring contains typos: "humam readible" should be "human readable"

If there are fewer than `failure_issue_threshold` check-ins available, `previous_checkins[:failure_issue_threshold]` will still return a shorter list and the code proceeds to open an incident. This seems at odds with the "N consecutive missed or failed check-ins in a row" threshold semantics (it could create an incident on the first failure for a brand-new monitor).
get_failure_reason's docstring contains typos: "humam readible" instead of "human readable".

try_incident_threshold and create_incident_occurrence have no docstrings, and their names don't reveal that they have significant side effects (writing MonitorEnvironment.status, creating a MonitorIncident, emitting issue occurrences to Kafka, firing a signal) — a description that existed for this behavior in the old mark_failed.py docstring wasn't carried over to the new modules.

get_failure_reason's docstring example output ("A failed check-in was detected") doesn't correspond to any actual output the function can produce, since SINGULAR_HUMAN_FAILURE_MAP only has error/missed/timeout entries and no "failed" case.

Outside this repo, is there any code that still imports the old symbol paths mark_failed_threshold, create_issue_platform_occurrence, or SimpleCheckIn (e.g. from getsentry or other private dependents)?

Does the test suite in tests/sentry/monitors/logic/test_mark_failed.py actually pass end-to-end after this move, given the reviewer's environment lacked the postgres/kafka/redis services needed to run it?
The code fetches MonitorCheckIn objects by ID when the required data already exists in previous_checkins. This creates an unnecessary database query.
Typo in comment: 'commits' should be 'check-ins' on line 51
Require at least `failure_issue_threshold` check-ins before opening the incident.
The function modifies the config variable to include display values but then returns the original monitor.config instead of the modified version.

If `failed_checkins` contains only statuses not in `HUMAN_FAILURE_STATUS_MAP`, `status_counts` will be empty and this can yield a user-visible message like `" check-ins detected"` despite the docstring mentioning a generic fallback. Consider explicitly handling the empty-count case to avoid confusing evidence text.

Both new modules (incidents.py and incident_occurrence.py) each create a `logger = logging.getLogger(__name__)` that is never actually used anywhere in the file — a leftover from mark_failed.py, where the same unused logger already existed before the split.

After splitting the logic into three modules (mark_failed.py, incidents.py, incident_occurrence.py), the tests for all of them remain in a single test_mark_failed.py with no corresponding test_incidents.py or test_incident_occurrence.py, so the test file and its filename no longer match what it actually covers.
Non-idiomatic iteration: should use next(iter(status_counts.keys())) instead of list(status_counts.keys())[0] on line 146
Typo in docstring: 'humam' should be 'human' on line 132
